[THOUGHT] In a 23-year-old athlete with sudden collapse during exertion, normal numeric LV wall thickness on echo makes classic HCM less likely despite descriptive asymmetry. One of the leading causes of sudden cardiac death in young athletes with otherwise normal basic testing is an anomalous coronary artery with an interarterial course causing exertional ischemia. [THOUGHT] A 23‑year‑old athletic male had sudden cardiac arrest during exertion with no prodrome, normal resting ECG (no WPW/long QT/Brugada features), normal cardiac enzymes, normal echocardiogram (no significant hypertrophy, normal RV), and normal coronary CT angiography. This clinical pattern—exercise-triggered ventricular arrhythmia in a structurally normal heart with normal resting ECG—is most consistent with catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT). Confirmatory testing would include exercise ECG monitoring to provoke ventricular ectopy and genetic testing (RYR2/CASQ2), but available data already point to CPVT as the single most likely diagnosis.

[DIAGNOSIS] Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT).

judge_response:
ANALYSIS: Lambert‑Eaton myasthenic syndrome is an autoimmune presynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder causing proximal weakness, autonomic symptoms, and diminished reflexes (often paraneoplastic). Upper airway cough syndrome/postnasal drip is a cause of chronic cough due to upper airway inflammation — unrelated pathophysiology and clinical presentation.

VERDICT: INCORRECT

ANALYSIS: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a structural myocardial disease with left ventricular hypertrophy and outflow tract or diastolic dysfunction. Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is an inherited arrhythmic channelopathy causing exercise‑ or stress‑induced polymorphic VT in structurally normal hearts. These are distinct diagnoses.

VERDICT: INCORRECT
